receipt.public_excerpt: When developers are allowed to use AI tools, they take 19% longer to complete issues—a significant slowdown that goes against developer beliefs and expert forecasts. This gap between perception and reality is striking: developers expected AI to speed them up by 24%, and even after experiencing the slowdown, they still believed AI had sped them up by 20%.

evidence_items.explanation: This is METR's 2025 study, and it reports the 19% slowdown and the 24% expected speedup Zitron cites. The only difference is that 24% was what developers expected beforehand. Afterwards they believed AI had sped them up by 20%.

receipt.public_excerpt: We do not claim that our developers or repositories represent a majority or plurality of software development work

evidence_items.explanation: METR limits the result to its sample of experienced open-source developers. That matters if 'engineers' is read as all engineers.

receipt.public_excerpt: we believe it is likely that developers are more sped up from AI tools now — in early 2026 — compared to our estimates from early 2025.

evidence_items.explanation: Published two days before the post, this says METR thinks the early-2025 result probably understates the speedup from newer tools. It does not change what the 2025 study found.
